The Representative Consumer

This scene asks whether many people can act as one. Shuffle money between two people with identical tastes.

However the money is split, aggregate demand never moves. What one person loses, the other gains exactly. Only the total amount of money matters. Then a representative consumer exists. The whole market computes like one imaginary person.

For example, twin brothers split a 💰 allowance of 12,000 won. The older may take 8,000 and the younger 4,000. Swap the split, and the 🍎 apples they buy stay the same. Only the total matters, not who holds what.
